rules.rule: Never re-pin the decoder version based on a README file.
Before re-pinning the decoder, read what the built binary links (e.g., run `nm halyard.elf | grep -c nvtegra` or check `ffversion.h`).
Do not investigate the :11020 port (STFP stats/keepalive) when working on Shadow image quality or resolution.
Before pushing a new shadow-client.nro to the Switch, remove the existing file with gio remove.
Do not delete the obsolete memory file about YUV_COMPOSITE and IDR_INJECT; keep it for historical traceability of the reverse-engineering work.
Only look at `var/report/` for Magento-level fatals after ruling out the missing mod_headers cause.
Place production-bound DB migration scripts under `migrations/`.
Place local-only DB fixup scripts under `scripts/local-dev/`.
Before pushing a phtml change that gates a new section on PHP variables, grep the file for every variable referenced in the new block.
Before pushing a phtml change that gates a new section on PHP variables, confirm that each variable referenced in the new block is assigned earlier in the same template.
Run `task docker:publish` only when the user explicitly asks for it.
Run `task docker:publish` only after the user has run `docker login` themselves.
Publish the dev image (`task docker:publish:dev` or `dev-image.yml`) only with the user's explicit go-ahead.
Do not compile anything in the Docker image build; it only packages prebuilt output.
Never scrape the EAN-Search public site, because its terms forbid automated queries and it has bot protection.
Before writing or editing any Go code, load the write-go skill, every time.
Never work around a Cloudflare challenge from CeX.
Never work around the Cloudflare challenge blocking CeX search (/v3/boxes?q=).
Do not blur or replace the README home page screenshot (docs/images/home.jpg) on your own.
Run the SteamGridDB provider only in the fallback pass, never as LinksOnly.
When probing the Telegram Bot API, use only a made-up (bogus) token, never real bot credentials.
The host's old `web/node_modules` directory may be deleted, since the container uses its own `node_modules` in a Docker volume.
Never run `golangci-lint run --fix` without limiting it to specific linters.
Enable developer mode via developerPrivate.updateProfileConfiguration before reloading the extension in end-to-end tests.
Never commit photo files to the repository.
When resuming the cover-recognition spike, start from the "Before building it" list in its README.
Have the user confirm the final game match before accepting it.
You may freely modify the Hermes reference install at ~/.hermes, since it is for reference rather than use.
Before creating any branch, open an issue for the work first, then create the branch from that issue.
Never delete a branch on your own initiative, except branches just merged as part of the release cleanup checklist.
Run `git push origin --delete <branch>` only after the user confirms or as part of post-release cleanup.
Name phase work branches as `phase-N-short-description`.
Always target the Development branch when opening a GitHub PR, never main.
Never close an issue until the user explicitly says they are happy with it.
Only run gh issue close after the user has confirmed.
Create branches from `Development` unless the user explicitly instructs otherwise.
Never close a GitHub issue without the user's explicit sign-off.
Run `gh issue close` only after the user confirms satisfaction with the work.
For new phases or significant features, wait for the user's explicit go-ahead before writing any code.
Do not treat finishing the Q&A as permission to start building; wait for the explicit go-ahead.
Never create a branch from `main`.
Never start building after Q&A alone; wait for the explicit go-ahead.
When opening a pull request, always target the Development branch for testing, never main.
On every `gh pr create` invocation, always pass `--base Development`.
Never use `--base main` when creating a pull request.
Do not open a pull request unless the user explicitly says to; when in doubt, ask the user first.
When opening a feature branch PR, always target the Development branch as the base, never main.
Merge feature→Development PRs only after the user has reviewed and approved them.
Open a Development→main PR only when the user says they are happy with a phase and it can go to main.
Never merge a Development→main PR; wait for the user to merge it themselves.
